data.name: Player shaped monsters choose a player attack
data.value: A player-shaped monster chooses a player attack from its equipment; attacks do not apply to it.

data.name: The monster has no attacks; it plays the generic pattern.
data.value: The monster has no attacks: it plays attack 1, attack 2, attack 2 (the generic pattern).

data.name: No code reads these attacks.
data.value: No handler reads these attacks: they do nothing until code reads them.

data.name: Monster skills note
data.value: The monster skill of packet 0x69; the game plays an attack for skills 1 to 77.

data.name: Player skills note
data.value: The player skill of packets 0x19 and 0x1E: 0x1E plays the attack at once; after 0x19 most skills play on the next normal attack (0x18), which reads the stored skill.

data.name: The game does not play an attack for this skill.
data.value: packet 0x69 plays no attack for this skill

data.name: Sound events note
data.value: Sounds the game plays on top of the slots for a character in one of an event's animations: when an attack starts, when it is hit or dies, at each step and at the end of each idle loop, within 500 units of the hero. An event plays sounds of this model.

data.name: Sound event death effect note
data.value: Only while the character's death effect is armed (the Snowman's death).

data.name: Sound event pick note
data.value: Plays the first of two sounds when a draw of one in two comes up, else the second; needs two sounds.

data.name: Sound event needs a sound of the model
data.value: An event plays sounds of this model, and it loads none.

data.name: Attack sound note
data.value: A SOUND_ id the attacks play each time they play (the traps'); empty: none.

data.name: Attack sound unknown
data.value: not a SOUND_ id the monster data can name

data.name: Monster model player note
data.value: A player-shaped monster: the game draws it as a player character, with the player's model, animations and the items its code gives it, some with a skin of their own (the skeletons' bodies). Its look still comes from the code; the model list holds monster and NPC models.

data.name: Monster model map object note
data.value: The monster appears as object {0} of its map (a trap): the map loads that model, not the model list.

data.name: Monster model other area note
data.value: The monster appears with {0}, a model of another area (the Kalima gates, the soccer ball): the model list holds monster and NPC models.

data.name: Preview volume note
data.value: The volume of the monster tools' sound previews (Play, the preview's sounds). The game's sound volume stays as it is, and this is not saved.
